newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S UNICBANK RAISES CAPITAL TO 7 BLN FORINTS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S UNICBANK RAISES CAPITAL TO 7 BLN FORINTS.

text.p: Hungary's Unicbank Rt, a banking unit of Austria's Raiffeisen group, raised its registered capital to seven billion forints from 4.36 billion, a Unicbank official told Reuters on Monday.

Attila Tajthy, head of the bank's legal department said that the extraordinary meeting of Unicbank's shareholders held earlier on Monday decided to increase the registered capital from the profit reserves, which will be reduced to 1.7 billion forints according to the Hungarian accounting standards.
The capital increase will not change the ownership structure of the bank, Tajthy added.
Unicbank said earlier that the capital increase would support its expansion plans in Hungary.
Unicbank plans either to buy Mezobank, which is active in retail banking and is to be privatised next year, or to expand the number of its own branches.
Unicbank is 96 percent owned by Raiffeisen.
Tajthy added that the shareholders also decided on Monday to change the bank's name to Raiffeisen Unicbank Rt, which better reflects the bank's international background.
